task: A diagnosis of the struct packing problem and a fix with explicit padding control.

criteria.text: Explains native alignment: with no prefix, struct uses native ('@') mode, which pads after the 1-byte bool so the double starts on an 8-byte boundary; the record is 4 + 1 + 3 (padding) + 8 = 16 bytes on common platforms, not 13.

Explains when values read incorrectly: data written with one layout (another platform, another compiler, or a packed 13-byte format) and read with another, which misaligns the fields or fails (struct.error on a length mismatch). A round trip on the same machine with the same format works.

The fix specifies the layout explicitly: a standard-size prefix with a byte order ('<', '>', '!' or '=') giving 13 bytes, or explicit pad bytes such as '<I?3xd' giving 16 bytes; pack and unpack use the same format.
Shows the fixed version round-trips the record and reports the size it now has (13, or 16 with explicit padding).
Mentions byte order (endianness) as part of portability.

reference: 'I?d' native: I at 0 (4), ? at 4 (1), 3 pad bytes, d at 8 (8): calcsize = 16. '<I?d': 13 bytes, no padding, little-endian. '<I?3xd': 16 bytes, explicit padding.
notes: Saying the native round trip on one machine 'corrupts values' without the cross-layout condition does not meet c2.
